deities: Baba Panchanan (five-faced form of Shiva; folk deity of Bengal)

history.period: unknown (one unverified online account calls a Howrah Baba Panchanan shrine about 150 years old)
history.summary: IDENTITY PROVISIONAL: several shrines named Baba Panchananda Mandir exist across Howrah district (Khurut/Andul, Dahuka-Nischindipur, Chamrail, Bira Chak, Belanagar) and the CSV gives no locality, so the intended shrine cannot be fixed. This entry documents the Khurut/Naora (Shibpur) shrine near Andul bus stand, the best-reviewed of them (local reviews call it the oldest temple of its neighbourhood). Baba Panchanan is the five-faced Shaivite folk deity widely worshipped in rural Bengal. One visitor review associates the Khurut shrine with Shani (Boro Baba/Sani Maharaj) - conflicting and unverified. No reliable published history found; coordinates are approximate (street-level geocode of the shrine's address).

name: Baba Panchananda Mandir
town_description: Howrah is the twin city of Kolkata across the Hooghly river, a major railway and industrial hub of West Bengal. Its pilgrimage landscape includes Belur Math (the Ramakrishna Order headquarters), and a dense network of old neighbourhood Kali and Shiva shrines such as the many Baba Panchanan temples of the district.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~35 km) (verify)
travel.road: Near Andul bus stand, off Nimai Sadhan Bose Sarani, Naora, Shibpur; reachable by road from central Howrah

visitor_information.opening_hours: Local reviews report 10 AM-2 PM and 7-8:30 PM (verify)
